mississippi.name: Mississippi
mississippi.agency: Mississippi State Department of Health, Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program

claims.claim: Mississippi runs a medical cannabis program, the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program (MMCP), under the Mississippi State Department of Health.
claims.quote: The Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program (MMCP) provides a safe and accessible program that meets the needs of patients ... The Mississippi State Department of Health is committed to meeting the statutory requirements

claims.claim: A registered practitioner certifies the qualifying condition, and the Mississippi State Department of Health issues the medical cannabis identification card.
claims.quote: they must be a licensed practitioner (MD, DO, Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, or Optometrist) that has been registered with the Mississippi State Department of Health ... The MS State Department of Health actually issues the medical cannabis identification cards to patients.

claims.claim: For patients under 18, the certification can only come from a physician (MD/DO), and the custodial parent or legal guardian must be a qualified caregiver. A designated caregiver must be at least 21.
claims.quote: A certification issued for a minor (under the age of 18) may only be issued by a physician (MD/DO). ... for people under the age of 18, the custodial parent or legal guardian must be a qualified caregiver. ... A "designated caregiver" is a person, at least 21 years of age

claims.claim: A resident cardholder may obtain no more than 24 MMCEUs of medical cannabis in 30 days, from one dispensary or a combination of dispensaries.
claims.quote: A resident cardholder shall not obtain more than a total of twenty-four (24) MMCEUs of allowable medical cannabis in thirty (30) days from a dispensary or a combination of dispensaries.

claims.claim: The possession limit is 28 MMCEUs for resident cardholders and 14 MMCEUs for nonresident cardholders.
claims.quote: A maximum of twenty-eight (28) MMCEUs is the possession limit for resident cardholders. The maximum possession limit for nonresident cardholders shall be fourteen (14) MMCEUs.

claims.claim: The law does not authorize using medical cannabis in a public place or in a motor vehicle.
claims.quote: The law does not authorize you to use medical cannabis in a public place or in a motor vehicle.

claims.claim: Registered patients must keep their registry identification card with them, especially when travelling to or from a licensed dispensary.
claims.quote: As a registered patient, you must always keep your registry identification card with you, especially when traveling to or from a licensed dispensary.

claims.claim: A Mississippi medical cannabis card is only valid in Mississippi.
claims.quote: No, your medical cannabis card is only valid in Mississippi.

claims.claim: Marijuana is legal for medical use in Oklahoma.
claims.quote: Although marijuana is legal for medical use in Oklahoma

claims.claim: Oklahoma residents aged 18 and up are eligible for an adult patient license from the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority (OMMA); residents aged 17 and younger are eligible for a minor patient license.
claims.quote: Oklahoma residents age 18 and up are eligible for a medical marijuana adult patient license ... Oklahoma residents age 17 and younger are eligible for a medical marijuana minor patient license

claims.claim: At one time, a licensed patient can legally possess up to 3 oz. of marijuana on their person and up to 8 oz. in their residence.
claims.quote: At one time, licensed patients can legally possess: ... Up to 3 oz. (84.9 g) of marijuana on their person ... 8 oz. (226.4 g) of marijuana in your residence

claims.claim: A licensed patient can also possess up to 1 oz. of concentrated marijuana, 72 oz. of edible marijuana, 72 oz. of topical marijuana, 6 mature plants and 6 seedling plants.
claims.quote: 6 mature marijuana plants and the harvested marijuana ... 6 seedling plants ... 1 oz. (28.3 g) of concentrated marijuana ... 72 oz. (2,037.6 g) of edible marijuana ... 72 oz. of topical marijuana

claims.claim: Smoking and vaping medical marijuana outdoors in public, or indoors at a workplace, is subject to the same state laws as smoking tobacco.
claims.quote: Smoking and vaping medical marijuana products outdoors in public (or indoors at a workplace) is subject to the same state laws as smoking tobacco.

claims.claim: Since November 1, 2025 (SB 518), medical marijuana labels must carry the warning: "It is illegal to drive a motor vehicle while under the influence of marijuana or marijuana products."
claims.quote: It is illegal to drive a motor vehicle while under the influence of marijuana or marijuana products.

claims.claim: The Oklahoma Highway Safety Office says drugged driving is still impaired driving, and that some people may be impaired for more than five hours after using marijuana.
claims.quote: Drugged or buzzed driving is still impaired driving. ... Some people may be impaired for more than five hours after using marijuana

claims.claim: Maryland voters approved adult-use cannabis in the 2022 General Election; since July 1, 2023, a person 21 or older may lawfully possess and use cannabis.
claims.quote: Maryland voters approved a ballot referendum in the 2022 General Election to allow use of cannabis by adults 21+ (hence, "adult-use") starting July 1, 2023. ... Effective July 1, 2023, a person 21 years or older may lawfully possess and use cannabis.

claims.claim: The legal purchase age for cannabis in Maryland is 21 or older.
claims.quote: Like tobacco and alcohol, the legal purchase age for cannabis in Maryland is 21 or older.

claims.claim: Licensed dispensaries are the only place to legally buy cannabis in Maryland.
claims.quote: Licensed dispensaries are the only place to legally buy cannabis in Maryland.

claims.claim: Adults 21 and older may possess up to 1.5 ounces of cannabis flower, up to 12 grams of concentrated cannabis, or cannabis products with no more than 750 mg of THC in total.
claims.quote: Adults 21 years and older may possess up to 1.5 ounces of cannabis flower, up to 12 grams of concentrated cannabis; or a total amount of cannabis products that does not exceed 750 mg of THC.

claims.claim: Smoking cannabis (and hemp) is prohibited in any public place, including parks, streets and sidewalks, and public transportation.
claims.quote: Smoking cannabis (and hemp) is prohibited in any public place. This includes outdoor spaces and indoor spaces open to the public including parks, streets and sidewalks, ... public transportation (e.g, buses, vans, trains, taxicabs, limousines)

claims.claim: Using cannabis while driving (by a driver or a passenger) and impaired driving remain illegal under Maryland law.
claims.quote: Using cannabis while driving (by a driver or passenger) and impaired driving remains illegal under Maryland law.

claims.claim: It is illegal to leave or enter Maryland with any cannabis products, medical or adult-use.
claims.quote: It remains illegal to leave (or enter) Maryland with any cannabis products - medical or adult-use (non-medical) products.

claims.claim: Maryland's medical cannabis program continues alongside adult-use, and a medical card is still needed to buy cannabis sold as part of the medical program.
claims.quote: The new law does not directly impact the medical cannabis program. ... A medical card is still needed to purchase cannabis sold as part of the medical cannabis program.

new-york.name: New York
new-york.agency: New York State Office of Cannabis Management (OCM)

claims.claim: The Marijuana Regulation & Taxation Act (MRTA), an act of the New York legislature, legalized adult-use cannabis.
claims.quote: The Marijuana Regulation & Taxation Act (MRTA) was an act of the legislature which legalized adult-use cannabis.

claims.claim: You have to be 21 to buy, consume or possess cannabis in New York State.
claims.quote: You have to be 21 to buy, consume, or possess cannabis in New York State.

claims.claim: Adults 21 or older may possess 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 grams of cannabis concentrate.
claims.quote: It is legal for adults 21 years or older to possess 3 ounces of cannabis and 24 grams of cannabis concentrate.

claims.claim: Businesses must have an adult-use license to legally sell cannabis in New York.
claims.quote: Businesses must have an adult-use license to legally sell cannabis in New York.

claims.claim: Adults may consume cannabis in a private home or in most places tobacco can be consumed, but not in a motor vehicle, a private business such as a restaurant patio, or any place where smoking tobacco is prohibited.
claims.quote: It is legal for adults 21 years or older to consume cannabis in a private home or in most places tobacco can be consumed, with the exception of consumption in a motor vehicle, a private business (such as a restaurant patio) ... It is illegal to use cannabis in a motor vehicle, a private business, or any place that smoking tobacco is prohibited

claims.claim: It is illegal to drive under the influence of cannabis.
claims.quote: It is illegal to drive under the influence of cannabis

claims.claim: Open containers of cannabis are illegal in a vehicle, and neither the driver nor any passenger may smoke cannabis in a vehicle, moving or parked.
claims.quote: It is illegal to have open containers of cannabis in a vehicle. It is illegal for the driver or any passengers to smoke cannabis while in a vehicle- moving or parked.

claims.claim: New York also runs a medical cannabis program, and there is no fee to become a patient in it.
claims.quote: There is no fee to become a patient in the program.
